title: Primitive integral operation comparisons are the specified counit transposes
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R$, uniformizer $t$, and $A_n=R/t^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For finite-type $k$-schemes $W$ work on their small pro-etale sites and put $\widehat R_W=\lim_n(A_n)_W$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let $\mathcal R_W\dashv\mathcal L_W$ be the actual reduction/total-limit adjunction on ordinary derived categories of strict semilinear module systems, with unit $u$ and counit $e$ [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus], using the simultaneous section constructions [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. System operations are exact inverse image $P_v$, derived direct image $S_v$ with $P_v\dashv S_v$, exact open extension $J_j\dashv P_j$, and derived tensor. All maps $v$ are separated finite type; maps denoted $p$ are proper and opens $j$ are quasi-compact [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Integral operations $A_{\rm int}$ are completed pullback and tensor, proper direct image, and localized completed-ring open extension [def-pur-integral-derived-operations, def-weil-derived-direct-image, lem-sf-integral-open-reduction-comparison]. Inputs $K_i$ are derived-complete constructible integral complexes. Every input and intermediate system occurring in the assertion is normalized, has compatible etale-origin witnesses and constructible cohomology, and has cohomological and finite Tor amplitudes in common finite intervals [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed, def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower, def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness, def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude].

For a basic operation $A$ write $d_A:\mathcal L A(\mathcal R K_i)\xrightarrow{\sim}A_{\rm int}(K_i)$ for its defining strict reduction-tower identification, with two inputs for tensor and with $d_j$ fixed by [lem-sf-integral-open-reduction-comparison]. Write $r_A:\mathcal R A_{\rm int}(K_i)\to A(\mathcal R K_i)$ for the canonical coefficient comparison of [lem-fix-operation-reduction], using the specified $r_j$ for open extension. These maps and the canonical completed ringed-site structural maps are fixed independently, through the section-normalized constructions [def-sf-integral-system-operations, def-sf-integral-system-canonical-bridge].

For each single $A=P_v,S_p,J_j$ or tensor, its specified coefficient comparison is the adjunction transpose of $d_A^{-1}$, as a natural equality of whole derived semilinear-system maps:
$$r_A=e_{A(\mathcal R K_i)}\circ\mathcal R(d_A^{-1}).$$
For pullback, tensor and proper image, the quotient-complex/total-limit models defining $d_A$ identify $d_A^{-1}$ with the defining tower realization map. In these coordinates the specified $r_A$ is the scalar-extension adjoint of the actual total-limit projection at each $n$, with the strict quotient transitions retained. For open extension, the specified identifications satisfy
$$d_j^{-1}=\mathcal L(r_j)\circ u_{j_!K},\qquad
 e_{J_j\mathcal R K}\circ\mathcal R\mathcal L(r_j)\circ\mathcal R(u_{j_!K})=r_j.$$
All equalities are natural in every input in the stated domain and hold before finite evaluation; the asserted identification is of the specified whole-system maps.

source.place: The maps-used sentence beginning “The maps used here are tensor reassociation, evaluation, and adjunction units and counits”; primitive transpose identification (returned proof step 2)

proof.text: Split the word by its constructor. The length-at-most-one bound forces every immediate child to have length zero, hence to be an input or unit; its primitiveFormulas proposition is True. Inputs and units themselves also have proposition True.

For tensor and pullback use the canonical quotient-augmentation identities and invertibility of their reduced completion maps. For any adjunction F⊣G, augmentation chi:X→Y, d:Y→G N, and r:F X→N, the identity chi≫d=u_X≫G(r) transposes to F(chi)≫F(d)≫e_N=r. Cancel the invertible F(chi). This gives exactly inverseOrZero(F(chi)) followed by r, the independently defined coefficient comparison.
For proper image pushR is the actual counit by definition. Reduction maps the identity in the asserted right side to the identity, so the formula is immediate.

For open extension, openDInv is definitionally u followed by L(openR). The inverse Hom-equivalence identity gives the counit-transpose formula for every input. A length-zero child is an admissible input or the coefficient unit. Open reconstruction effectivity supplies invertibility of the fixed open reduction mate and the actual unit. Replace inverseOrZero by inv and cancel each pair of inverse maps to get both inverse laws.
